original_test_intent: Verify the exact Mellanox BF4 board and its authorized board-side connections can be serviced once without damage, then return correctly seated with the same FRU, PCIe/function inventory and qualified link/health state.
original_method: Bind this variant by row/hash in addition to the colliding code; identify BF4 PN/serial/revision, slot, retention and board-side connector/cable scope; preserve photos and PCIe/BF4 state; isolate power and use ESD/torque controls; technician performs one approved board/connector action; restore and verify the identical BF4 functions, expected links, firmware/driver state and no new AER/BMC/host faults.
manual_activity: A qualified technician services the specifically identified BF4 board/approved connector scope once under vendor power, ESD and retention controls.
required_inputs: Variant-specific replacement for the code collision or permanent row/hash identity rule
BF4 PN/serial/revision, slot and board-side connector/cable action list
Vendor power isolation, ESD, retention/torque and handling procedure
Expected BF4 PCIe BDF/functions, link attributes, firmware/driver and health/error oracle
safety_requirements: Do not select this case by code alone; require row and variant ID
Power isolate/discharge and use ESD controls before BF4 board handling
Define one board/connector action; never interpret all components as unrestricted cycling
Stop on damage, resistance, retention mismatch, power fault, missing function, link degradation or new error
Preserve logs and do not repeat/reseat automatically
agent_execution_scope: Enforce row/variant identity and exclude Serial Port evidence
Validate BF4 FRU/service scope, handling gates and electronic oracle
Collect unique pre/post BF4 inventory/link/error artifacts and technician photos
Do not handle hardware, clear logs, choose recovery or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve the duplicate-code ownership while preserving both rows
Approve exact BF4 board/connector action, power/ESD/retention procedure and recovery
Review row-specific physical/electronic evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master assigns Wistron-HW-00473-V002 to both row 1978 Serial Port mechanical check and row 2193 Mellanox BF4 Board. Row/hash/variant makes this review reliable, but code-only identity is ambiguous and requires engineering remediation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The BF4 row identity and manual purpose are reliable through the variant ID. The code collision and service details can be recorded pending without blocking static review.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2193 Wistron-HW-00473-V002: assign or approve a unique authoritative identity distinct from row 1978 Serial Port; approve BF4 PN/serial/revision/slot and exact board-side component/connectors to service, vendor power-isolation/ESD/retention/torque procedure, pre/post PCIe function/link/AER and BF4 firmware/driver/health oracle, log/photo preservation, aborts, and recovery ownership.

review_improvement: Prevents same-code cross-execution and turns the BF4 board row into a bounded physical action with full-function electronic recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: This row's code cannot safely select a test because row 1978 uses it for a Serial Port. The manifest variant resolves the current source, so review may continue only with composite identity. For the BF4 board itself, generic detection is too weak: a multi-function accelerator/DPU can enumerate partially or at a degraded PCIe link. Physical seating, retention and touched connectors must be correlated with complete function/link/health evidence after one controlled service cycle.
